idiom_name: one-line per-type function / GNU statement-expression macro ID(x), plus the qsort identity comparator
implementation_notes: ISO C has no polymorphic functions, so the classic ∀a. a→a cannot be written generically: the realization collapses into a one-line function per concrete type — e.g. int id_int(int x) { return x; } — which the compiler inlines at -O1 and above, leaving zero call overhead in direct calls. GNU C gets closest to a polymorphic identity with a statement-expression macro #define ID(x) ({ __auto_type id_x_ = (x); id_x_; }), which evaluates x exactly once and preserves its exact expression type (typeof/__auto_type capture it at compile time); C11 _Generic is the type-domain companion for selecting per-type identities, but it is a compile-time selection, not a runtime generic function. The classic form remains justified where a genuine function pointer of erased type is required: qsort(3) needs a real int (*)(const void *, const void *) comparator (passing NULL is undefined behaviour), so int ident_cmp(const void *a, const void *b){(void)a; (void)b; return 0;} serves as the neutral 'no derived key' comparator.
pitfalls: A naive #define ID(x) (x) multi-evaluates its argument: ID(next_counter()) advances the counter twice. The GNU statement-expression form with __auto_type evaluates x exactly once — the same reason GCC's own docs give for statement-expression max macros.

Statement expressions, __auto_type and typeof are GNU extensions, not ISO C, and a statement expression is not allowed in constant expressions (enumeration values, bit-field widths, static initializers) — ID(SOME_CONST) cannot initialize a static object; gate with __GNUC__ or fall back to per-type functions.

A comparator identity is type-erased: qsort hands the callback const void *, and the compiler cannot check that the comparator's inverse cast matches the element type — sorting an array of int * with an int-comparing comparator silently compares pointers. Returning a-b instead of a three-way compare is additionally undefined on signed overflow.

An identity comparator that returns 0 for every pair does not mean 'stable pass-through': POSIX and the qsort(3) man page leave the order of equal elements unspecified, so the sorted output may be a permutation of the input even though nothing compared unequal.

Function pointers carry no closure: there is no way to bind state to an identity function as in Java's Function.identity(); context must travel through void * (qsort_r's arg, itself a GNU/POSIX extension) or file-scope globals, which breaks reentrancy across threads.

Through a function-pointer parameter (a qsort compar argument) the call is indirect and will not be inlined; passing identity through such an interface in a hot loop costs an indirect call per element, unlike the directly-called static one-liner.
